comparison: Perfect agreement on combinatorial expression patterns (C2-C8, C31). Both evaluations find the single-cell sequencing methodology innovative and the findings well-supported. All three peer reviewers explicitly affirm the methodological advance and confirm the results align with previous findings.

Strong agreement on Pcdhg cKO connectivity findings (C9-C16, C32). Both evaluations support the electrophysiological evidence showing increased connectivity in knockout mice. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'solid' and 'convincing' data, though peer review also incorporates broader contextual claims (C44, C54, C59) not grouped with this result by OpenEval.

OpenEval evaluates Pcdha cKO negative control (C13) separately as supporting specificity. Peer review groups this with other knockout findings in R2, affirming the overall experimental approach without separately highlighting this negative control.

Both agree on successful overexpression validation (C17-C20), but peer review R3 encompasses broader claims including differential isoform effects (C21-C24, C33, C46, C52, C53) that OpenEval separates into R5 and R6. Peer reviewers note caveats about reliance on overexpression and lack of protein level demonstration.

Both support differential effects of variable vs C-type isoforms (C21-C22, C24, C33, C46). OpenEval emphasizes the large effect size and statistical significance. Peer review acknowledges these findings but notes limitations of overexpression approach and focus on C4 rather than other isoforms.

Both support the rescue experiment findings (C23, C52). OpenEval highlights this as strong evidence for variable isoform specificity. Peer review incorporates this within broader overexpression results, accepting the conclusion while noting methodological limitations.

Strong agreement on dose-dependent similarity effects (C25-C30, C34, C48, C50, C62-C63). Both evaluations emphasize the sophisticated sequential electroporation design. Peer reviewers call the methodology 'impressive' and accept the main result. OpenEval includes C28 here while peer review groups it separately; peer review also includes mechanistic interpretation claims (C64, C74) that OpenEval evaluates separately in R9.

OpenEval separately evaluates the critical control showing no effect on electroporated-control pairs (C28). Peer review incorporates this within the broader similarity-dependent findings in R4, implicitly accepting its importance for demonstrating similarity-based rather than expression-based effects.

Both support the mechanistic conclusion about homophilic matching as negative regulator (C35, C51, C64). OpenEval notes the cellular mechanism remains undetermined. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the 'impressive' demonstration of this previously-reported finding, though note that necessity of isoform diversity in physiological conditions requires further clarification.

Perfect agreement on methodological advance (C39). Both evaluations affirm the improved method for detecting clustered protocadherin transcripts. Peer reviewer explicitly states the method 'should be applicable more broadly' and is worth publishing.

Both address comparisons to prior studies (C40-C45). OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without direct experimental evidence. Peer review accepts the contextual discussion, acknowledging differences from other studies remain unresolved but that future genetic approaches should help clarify.

OpenEval evaluates C-type isoform functional differences (C47) as supported inference from literature synthesis. Peer review incorporates this within broader contextual claims in R7, accepting the discussion without specific comment on this particular inference.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic context from prior work (C49) as appropriately cited. Peer review includes this among contextual claims in R7, accepting the literature discussion without challenging the interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates synthesis of differential isoform effects (C53) as supported conclusion. Peer review incorporates this within overexpression findings in R3, accepting the conclusion while noting it's based on limited isoform testing.

Both address regional heterogeneity synthesis (C54-C61). OpenEval finds the literature synthesis appropriate though not experimentally explored. Peer review accepts the discussion of regional differences, noting present findings don't resolve them but future genetic approaches should help.

Both address extensive prior literature context (C65-C73). OpenEval evaluates these as appropriately cited background claims. Peer review incorporates these among contextual claims in R7, accepting the literature characterization without dispute.
